events.credibility_reason: Single unreviewed preprint about six weeks old whose AI-use statements contradict each other; and it is about the stable forking conjecture, not Kueker's.
events.ai_basis: This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.

why: Every event that bears on Kueker's conjecture comes before the snapshot. Each one settles the conjecture for a class of theories (superstable; stable, interpreting a linear order, or with Skolem functions; weakly VC-minimal), so they are cases, not the whole statement. Hrushovski's thesis and his JSL paper are one argument, recorded twice: I scored both as cases. I left the thesis unreviewed because its committee is only inferred and is not named. Tanović 2012 restricts the structure of Kueker theories but proves no categoricity conclusion, so its scope is none. Shelah 2005 only uses known cases, so it is none too. Shami's 'Kueker simple' theories are a different question that shares the name, so that paper is a variant. Freitag–Mutchnik is about a different conjecture (stable forking), so it is a variant. Its AI role is marked generated from its own quote, but it does nothing for this problem.
doubts: The bullet gives only the name, so the statement is taken from the literature wording; Wikipedia's reference [156] was never reached. Hrushovski 1986 and 1989 are the same argument recorded as two events. The researcher could not query arXiv math.LO directly for 2024–2026 papers.
